title: Traffic replica simulator and rollback playbook for canary evaluations
author: Sanjay Patel
release_notes: Adds a traffic replica simulator for controlled canary replay and a documented rollback playbook that ties canary detectors to suggested remediation steps and automated paging hooks.
description:
Context & motivation: We frequently see noisy regressions blocked by the gap between synthetic probes and actual production traffic shapes. This PR adds a traffic replica simulator that can replay sampled production slices into a canary instance (isolated test replicas) so detectors evaluate real-world query shapes, KV cache warmup, and user session patterns. It pairs that simulator with a human-friendly rollback playbook that consolidates detector outputs into a prioritized remediation checklist and recommended automated actions (circuit, throttle, fallback model, or immediate rollback).

What this PR delivers (high-level): 1) A lightweight traffic replica runtime (perf_canary/simulator) that consumes sampled request traces (ndjson) and replays them with configurable concurrency/temporal scaling and header-preserving semantics. 2) Integration hooks from existing canary detectors to the simulator so we can run offline and live replays as part of evaluation pipelines. 3) A rollback playbook (docs/playbooks/rollback.md) with templated pager messages, escalation steps, and automated rollback recipes that can be executed from the Console or via the CLI. 4) End-to-end unit and integration tests and a small infra change to grant the canary agent permissions for ephemeral replay resources.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4412) - [x] Simulator API and config schema added - [x] Detector adapter implemented - [x] Rollback playbook drafted and reviewed by SRE - [x] Tests (unit/integration/ci) - [x] CI green, smoke-tested on staging

Commits summary: - feat(simulator): add replay engine and load-scaling controller - feat(adapters): detector -> simulator bridge + sampling util - docs(playbook): rollback playbook and escalation templates - test(ci): add deterministic replay fixture and integration test - chore(permissions): update canary-agent IAM roles

Changed areas / files (high level): - perf_canary/simulator/replica_runner.go (core replay loop and scaling controller) - perf_canary/simulator/config.go (replay configuration + templates) - perf_canary/adapters/detector_to_simulator.go (bridge that converts detector slices to replay sessions) - docs/playbooks/rollback.md (playbook and pager templates) - examples/replay-samples/ (ndjson trace samples and quickstart) - tests/integration/replay_end_to_end_test.go - infra/canary-agent/iam.yaml (ephemeral replay role) - console/hooks/playbook_action_handler.go (trigger from Console)

Review conversation (selected highlights): - Maya Alvarez (reviewer): "Great design. A few comments on concurrency jitter — prefer a Poisson arrival emulator for session starts to avoid synthetic synchronization spikes." - Author (Sanjay): "Addressed: switched the arrival generator to Poisson and added a deterministic seed for CI fixtures (see commit 3)." - Rohit Kapoor (reviewer): "Concern: permissions change looks a little broad. Can we scope the ephemeral role to replay-only S3 prefix?" - Author (Sanjay): "Narrowed permissions to example-replay/ prefix and added a short runbook in docs for operators." - Claire Huang (approver): "Playbook is clear — approved pending CI."

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass (100%) - integration-tests: pass (replay_end_to_end simulated against staging stack) - lint: pass (go vet, golangci-lint) - e2e-smoke: pass (manual smoke run on staging) Notes: initial CI run failed due to nondeterministic arrival generator; fixed by adding deterministic seed and updated tests to assert seed-driven metrics.

Performance/operational notes: - Simulator default replay uses 10% of sampled traffic by default with a configurable multiplier; this avoids overloading canary instances. - KV-cache warmup step included so canary detectors observe steady-state hit rates before metric collection window. - The detector->simulator integration exposes a "shadow" mode that runs without modifying routing for low-risk validation.

Rollout/merge plan: - Merged via squash (squash-and-merge) after approvals. - Gradual rollout: simulator enabled behind feature flag; playbook links added to canary run UI. - Suggested monitoring: add a short-term alert to watch replica CPU and token throughput when replay multiplier > 1.

How to test locally: - See examples/replay-samples/README.md for sample traces and a quickstart script: ./scripts/run-replay --trace examples/replay-samples/session_slice.ndjson --multiplier 0.1 - Use --dry-run to validate session translation without sending traffic.

Related work and references: - ENG-4412 (design doc) - SRE-219 (incident that motivated offline replay) - internal notes: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/perf/replay-design (private link)

Merge outcome: merged on 2026-03-02 via squash-and-merge. Post-merge tasks: create a canary feature flag ticket to enable simulator for 25% of canaries in staging (assigned to SRE).
